title: Alpha4 cross-dataset transfer test
research_question: Do the architecture principles promoted on ECG200 transfer to a second time-series classification problem without retuning Alpha4?
hypothesis: Frozen Alpha4 will remain competitive with the same fixed MLP calibration baseline on a second small univariate UCR/UEA time-series dataset, providing evidence that its compact k=[1,2] basis and 16-sample local receptive-field principle are not specific to ECG200.
scientific_boundary: This is a transfer test, not a new architecture search. Alpha4 topology, k=[1,2], optimizer, epochs and seed set are frozen before observing target TEST results.

transfer_design.rationale: Small canonical univariate UCR/UEA classification dataset with length 150, suitable for an inexpensive transfer test while differing from ECG morphology.
transfer_design.pnn_input_handling: Deterministically center-crop the 150-sample series to 144 samples so it divides into nine contiguous 16-sample windows. No learned or TEST-dependent preprocessing.
transfer_design.alpha4_transfer: 9 contiguous windows × 16 samples; each Q.ANT Fourier/KAN 16→16; concatenate 144 features; Q.ANT Fourier/KAN 144→2; k=[1,2]. The local block design and frequency basis are frozen; only the number of repeated windows and head input dimension adapt mechanically to input length.
transfer_design.mlp_calibration: Fixed two-hidden-layer MLP scaled mechanically to input length: 144→64→32→2.

data_protocol.test_usage: No candidate selection or hyperparameter tuning from TEST.

training_protocol.preprocessing: raw archive values after deterministic center crop 150→144

success_criteria: Transfer is supported if frozen Alpha4-transfer mean Q.ANT TEST accuracy is at least 0.90 and mean reference/Q.ANT prediction disagreements are <=1.0 per TEST set across seeds. MLP is calibration only and does not determine success.
promotion_rule: No architecture promotion occurs in Exp012. A successful result supports cross-dataset transfer and motivates a broader multi-dataset benchmark.
hardware_boundary: Software/simulation-backend experiment only; no real photonic hardware performance claim.
